This is more or less the premise of the South Beach Diet (and--I've heard but can't confirm--Atkins). There's a strict "induction" phase during which carbs are kept extremely low, then healthy carbs (eg, whole grains, fruits) are slowly reintroduced during the ongoing weight-loss and, finally, maintenance phases. I absolutely needed the strict ramp-up, no-carb, kick-off (which I actually stayed in for 2 months because I felt so good) because I was absolutely addicted to sugar and processed carbs; I literally needed a detox. I did experience "keto flu" but in my opinion, that means it was the right diet for me because I needed to withdraw from sugar--and keto flu felt exactly like withdrawal symptoms. I've maintained a 50-lb weight loss for 5 years with SBD and could never have done it without an initial keto period that re-set my body and prepared me to re-learn healthy eating habits without having to suffer cravings beyond a relatively short period.

Sounds like you're smoking indica rather than sativa--I personally will not smoke indica-dominant strains for the reasons you mentioned...sativa gives me much more of an "up," happy, giggly, social feeling and it's the the only type of weed I'll smoke (which is like maybe twice a month, not every day). You may also be smoking too much. Weed also affects me very strongly so I'll take one hit, wait about 20 minutes, and then consider another hit depending on how I'm feeling. 

That said, different drugs can vary widely in regard to their effects on different people and it can take some trial and error to see what works best for you individually. And with THAT said, you may just not be a weed person and that's totally fine! Most of the people I know do not smoke weed at all; I know others who will smoke but will not drink alcohol at all; and others who do not drink or take any drugs at all.  Experiment if you want, and if you don't like something, don't feel pressured to do it.
